source_text: De huius itaque legibus ita probari et vindicari non potest, quod esse constat iniustum, ut si hoc fieri posset, illius divinitas tota vilesceret. Ab eo igitur probabitur de Scripturis sanctis iniustitiae dogma firmari, a quo approbari quiverit Trinitatem, cui credimus, divinitatis gloria posse privari.
pass_a_gloss: About the laws of this one therefore that which stands as unjust cannot so be proved and vindicated, that if this could be done, his whole divinity would cheapen. By him therefore it will be proved that a dogma of injustice is made firm from the Holy Scriptures, by whom it could be approved that the Trinity, to whom we believe, can be deprived of the glory of divinity.
pass_b_english: It is therefore so impossible to prove and vindicate from his laws something known to be unjust that, if it could be done, his entire divinity would lose its worth. Only someone who could prove that the Trinity in whom we believe could be deprived of divine glory could prove that a doctrine of injustice is established by the Holy Scriptures.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Opposite of iustitia; Julian refuses a God whose ordinances establish injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
